themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Many of these problems stall because the person who holds the answer gains nothing by sharing it, and nobody can make them. So the models either try to make honesty pay better than hiding, or they stop waiting for cooperation and work only with what they already own.
themes.evidence: On cross-channel journey orchestration all three models said channel owners will quietly subvert any shared arbitration layer because their bonuses reward local volume; the same logic drives the agent fast-lane perks proposed for agentic traffic, the platform opacity blamed in incrementality measurement, and the black-box partners in downstream consent enforcement.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls are about meaning and worth, not data: whether a headline implies a promise, whether evidence really backs a claim, what one more message to a customer is actually worth. No formula settles these, because the disagreement has budget attached.
themes.evidence: On cross-channel journey orchestration Claude called any single objective function a political artifact rather than a measurement, echoing the contested definitions of customer in the semantic context layer work and the implied-claim judgments that block automated review of generative content.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what happens next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email, a spent dollar, or an exported list cannot be called back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: Today's answers on cross-channel journey orchestration all proposed one shared send log, a veto-only kill switch, or a hard contact cap; the same pattern appears as the agent proxy or gateway in safe agent execution and the single data exit gate in downstream consent enforcement.

themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Most of these problems have no answer key. There is no trustworthy record of who is really the same person, what an AI assistant would have said anyway, or what sales would have been without the ad, so the models start by building a small truth set they can grade themselves against.
themes.evidence: Claude proposed a person-level holdout across every channel to test whether coordination even helps in journey orchestration, mirroring the consented device panels in identity resolution, the fixed prompt panels in answer engine optimization, and the always-on geo holdouts in incrementality measurement.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, a message, or a dollar leaves your own systems, you cannot see inside the partner, ad platform, or trained model that now holds it. The best anyone offers is watching from outside: planting fake records, or expiring every list you send so nothing lives on by default.
themes.evidence: In downstream consent enforcement the models suggested canary profiles and fourteen-day list expiry because walled gardens and trained models cannot be read back, and similar outside-only inference shows up in agentic traffic detection and ad supply integrity.
